sentences.text: Ferganosuchus is an extinct genus containing only one species of gavialid crocodilian.
The genus Ferganosuchus was described by Efimov in 1982, and it is well known because fossils include fairly complete specimens, unlike the fragmentary remains of most other Asian tomistomines.

Ferganosuchus belongs to the family Gavialidae, and its parent group is the subfamily Tomistominae. Researchers classify Ferganosuchus as a tomistomine, though some suggest it might be a more basal gavialoid.
The type species of the genus Ferganosuchus is Ferganosuchus planus.
Fossils of Ferganosuchus have been found in Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan dating to the Middle Eocene.
